title: I Posted the Condo Dryer Hours the Super Claimed Did Not Exist

parts.text: I hauled a wet comforter to the basement at 8:04 p.m. because the posted sign said laundry until ten. The dryers were unplugged. A paper said CLOSED PER SUPER. I was twenty-nine, dripping rain on the concrete, holding a mesh bag that smelled like detergent and mildew. The super, Ray, answered on the third knock with a hockey game behind him. "We close at eight now. I told people." I asked where. He said, "Verbally." I photographed the laminated ten p.m. sign still screwed to the wall, the unplugged cords, and the wet comforter. In the group chat Ray wrote that I was trying to wake the building. I replied with the photo of the screws. Then I noticed the dryers were unplugged from a power strip that ran under Ray's storage cage, and the strip was humming like something else was using the circuit.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The dryers are unplugged into his cage; the laminated sign still says ten.

social.video_title: He unplugged the dryers and called it verbal policy — Part 1/2
social.description: Wet comforter, a hockey game, and a super who changed hours by voice. The power strip ran under his cage. Would you have waited until morning?

parts.text: I emailed the board with the photos and the original house rules PDF that still said 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Ray claimed he was preventing noise. The board asked why the power strip also fed a mini-fridge in his cage. He said it was medicine. The fridge was full of beer. They restored the hours, capped the cage circuit, and sent a notice that verbal policy is not policy. I dried the comforter at 8:40 the next night. It smelled like fabric softener instead of basement. Ray watches hockey with headphones now. The laminated sign got a second screw. I keep a quarter roll in a mug labeled TEN.

social.video_title: The mini-fridge was beer, not medicine — Part 2/2
social.description: House rules PDF, a humming strip, and a board that still knows how to read a clock. Was verbal ever a bylaw?
